extraction_text: 护民子讲述了尊者甘婆仙人在俱卢族会堂上对难敌的劝告。

attributes.relationships: 护民子转述甘婆仙人对难敌的劝告

extraction_text: 甘婆仙人阐述宇宙永恒与无常的法则，强调梵天、那罗、那罗延、毗湿奴永恒不灭，而其他万物包括国王都会死亡。

attributes.divine_elements: 提及梵天、那罗、那罗延、毗湿奴等神祇

extraction_text: 甘婆仙人劝告难敌与坚战和解，让般度族和俱卢族共同保护大地，并警告难敌不要自以为强大。

attributes.relationships: 甘婆仙人劝难敌与坚战和解，涉及般度族和俱卢族
attributes.key_plot: 核心劝诫，推动和平解决冲突

extraction_text: 甘婆仙人引用摩多梨嫁女选婿的传说作为例证。

attributes.relationships: 甘婆仙人用传说教育难敌

extraction_text: 摩多梨是天帝因陀罗的车夫，他有一个美丽女儿德髻到了出嫁年龄，摩多梨和妻子妙法为找不到合意女婿而烦恼。

attributes.relationships: 摩多梨是德髻的父亲、因陀罗的车夫；妙法是德髻的母亲

extraction_text: 摩多梨和妙法决定去蛇界寻找女婿，因为在天国和人间都找不到与德髻相配的人。

attributes.relationships: 夫妻共同为女儿婚事做决定

extraction_text: 摩多梨在途中遇见大仙人那罗陀，那罗陀询问他的目的，摩多梨如实告知是为自己的事前往伐楼拿那里。

attributes.relationships: 那罗陀是仙人，伐楼拿是水神；摩多梨寻求伐楼拿
attributes.divine_elements: 涉及仙人那罗陀和水神伐楼拿

extraction_text: 那罗陀提议与摩多梨一起去见伐楼拿，因为他自己也是从天上下来准备看望伐楼拿。

attributes.relationships: 那罗陀和摩多梨共同前往见伐楼拿

extraction_text: Narada and Matali descended to the underworld to find a suitable groom.
They met Varuna, the lord of waters and protector of the world, in the underworld.

attributes.details: Narada was honored like a celestial sage, Matali like Indra

extraction_text: With Varuna's permission, they toured the serpent realm (Naga-loka).
Narada described various beings and wonders of the underworld to Matali.
Narada pointed out Varuna's son Pushkara (also called Nilapadma), who was chosen as husband by Soma's daughter.

attributes.description: Blue-lotus eyed, wise, pure character surpassing his father

extraction_text: Narada showed Matali Varuna's golden palace and various divine weapons.

attributes.weapon_details: Weapons of defeated Daityas, Gandiva bow, Brahma's staff, Indra's weapons

extraction_text: Narada described Varuna's canopy that flows with cool water like rain clouds.

attributes.description: Flows with moon-pure water but darkened and invisible

extraction_text: Narada suggested they leave the underworld to avoid being distracted by its wonders.
Narada described the city of Patala in the center of the serpent realm, inhabited by Daityas and Danavas.

attributes.description: Where animals and inanimate objects flow in fearfully

extraction_text: Narada explained the Asura fire that feeds on water and the place where gods drink and store nectar.

attributes.explanation: Moon's phases are visible here because gods store nectar

extraction_text: The sacred horse head appears on new and full moons, shining with golden light and filling the world with water.

attributes.description: A divine celestial event involving a horse head that illuminates and provides water.

extraction_text: The city of Patala is named due to various forms of water falling there.

attributes.description: The city gets its name from water-related phenomena.

extraction_text: Airavata the elephant draws water here and pours it into clouds, enabling Indra to send cool rain.

attributes.description: Airavata supports Indra's rain-making by transferring water to clouds.

extraction_text: Large fish and aquatic animals live here, drinking moonlight in the water.

attributes.description: Describes the inhabitants of Patala and their unique sustenance.

extraction_text: Creatures on Patala's surface die from sun exposure by day but revive at night when moonrise brings nectar-like moonlight.

attributes.description: A daily cycle of death and revival tied to sunlight and moonlight.

extraction_text: Daityas who committed unlawful acts, stripped of wealth by Indra, are imprisoned here to suffer over time.

attributes.description: Indra punishes Daityas by imprisoning them in Patala.

extraction_text: Prajapati, the lord of all beings, performs supreme austerities here for the welfare of all beings.

attributes.description: Prajapati engages in intense penance for universal benefit.

extraction_text: Many great Brahmin sages who follow the cow vow, emaciated from studying scriptures, abandon life here and ascend to heaven.

attributes.description: Sages achieve liberation through rigorous vows and scriptural study.

extraction_text: Elephant kings Airavata, Vamana, Kumuda, and Anjana are born in the Subharadika (beautiful-faced) elephant clan.

attributes.description: Notable elephants are born into a specific clan.

extraction_text: Narada suggests to Matari that they search for a suitable son-in-law wherever they find satisfactory qualities.

attributes.description: Narada proposes a quest to find a worthy groom.

extraction_text: An egg placed in water shines auspiciously, unbroken and unmoving since creation, with unknown origin; at world's end, fire from it will burn all three worlds.

attributes.description: A mysterious egg with apocalyptic significance.

extraction_text: After hearing Narada's words, Matari says no one here satisfies him and urges to go elsewhere.

attributes.description: Matari rejects local options and decides to continue the search.

extraction_text: Narada describes the famous golden city, a great city where Daityas and Danavas with hundreds of illusions live, built by Vishvakarma with mental illusion power.

attributes.description: Narada details a city inhabited by powerful illusion-wielding beings.

extraction_text: In the past, immensely valiant Danavas obtained boons and lived here using thousands of illusions; Indra, Varuna, Yama, and Kubera could not subdue them.

attributes.description: Danavas, empowered by boons, resisted major deities.

extraction_text: Kalakanja Asuras arose from Vishnu's feet and Neneta monsters from Brahma's Vedas; they are fierce, illusion-wielding, and self-protective.

attributes.description: Describes the divine origins of specific demonic beings.

extraction_text: The fully-armored Danavas are known for battle frenzy that even Indra cannot withstand; Matari and his son Gomukha, as well as Indra and his son, have retreated before them.

attributes.description: Highlights the combat prowess of Danavas against deities.

extraction_text: Narada points out the exquisitely crafted golden and silver palaces to Matari.

attributes.description: Narada draws attention to the architectural marvels of the city.

extraction_text: Narada describes the world of the Garudas (great eagles) who eat snakes and are tireless in courage, flight, and bearing burdens.
Narada explains that this family descends from the six sons of Vinata's son (Garuda), named Shubhanana, Shubhanama, Shubhaksha, Shubhaprabha, Shubhavarna, and Shubhabala.

relationships: Six named Garudas are descendants of Garuda

extraction_text: Narada states these Garuda kings have produced thousands of generations, born in the Kashyapa family, enhancing family prosperity.

Narada describes the Garudas as auspicious, wealthy, bearing swastika marks, desiring wealth, and powerful. By behavior, they are Kshatriyas but cruelly eat snakes and, due to destroying relatives, haven't attained Brahminhood.

attributes.moral_aspect: Lack of Brahminhood due to destroying relatives

extraction_text: Narada explains the Garudas are praised because they revere Vishnu, who is their deity, refuge, always in their hearts, and their ultimate destination.
Narada lists numerous important Garuda names, including Suvarnashiras, Sarparashi, Dharuna, Tikshnatunda, Anala, Anila, Vipulaksha, Kundali, and many others.
Narada concludes by saying he has only listed some important, renowned, and respected Garudas, and suggests they leave if Matari doesn't like them.
